nodes.title: BSI TR-02102-1 (2026-01-23) + -2 TLS (2026-01-27): ML-KEM-768/1024, FrodoKEM, McEliece; hybrid-only; no X25519/Ed25519/ChaCha20 in TLS list
nodes.summary: Germany recommends PQ KEMs only hybridised ('currently only recommends hybrid use'); classical-only key agreement until end-2031, PQ by end-2030, classical signatures until end-2035. TLS 1.3 list has NIST/brainpool curves, AES-GCM/CCM only; BSI 'intends to recommend' SecP256r1MLKEM768 and SecP384r1MLKEM1024 (not X25519MLKEM768) after the RFC.
nodes.specifics: TR-02102-1 Tab 2.5/2.6/2.7: FrodoKEM-976/1344; mceliece460896/6688128/8192128(+f); ML-KEM-768/1024 (512 absent). Sig Tab 5.6/5.7: SLH-DSA-{SHA2,SHAKE}-192s/f,256s/f; ML-DSA-65/87 hedged (44 absent); LMS/HSS, XMSS/XMSS^MT; PQ sig only in concatenated hybrid with classical except hash-based (may be alone). Hybridisation KDFs: CatKDF (KMAC/HKDF), KeyCombine. QKD not recommended. TR-02102-2 Tab 10 groups: secp256/384/521r1, brainpoolP256/384/512r1tls13, ffdhe3072/4096 (to 2031); sig algs rsa_pss*, ecdsa_secp*r1 '2032+'; TLS1.3 suites AES_128/256_GCM, AES_128_CCM only (0 hits chacha/25519/Ed25519); 0-RTT not recommended; TLS1.2 until end-2031; RSA PKCS#1v1.5 sigs dropped in 2026-01. TR-02102-3 (IPsec) intends ml-kem-768/1024 hybrid; -4 (SSH) intends mlkem768nistp256-sha256 and mlkem1024nistp384-sha384. Language: EN official translation read; DE original exists (not read). Prediction: TR-02102-2 2027-01 edition adopts 0x11EB/0x11ED (RFC 10024 published Aug 2026), p~0.8.
nodes.overclaim_risk: TR is a recommendation, not law; binding via procurement/CC/KRITIS practice. Read EN translation not DE original.
nodes.underclaim_risk: BSI list not mentioning X25519 means 'not recommended', not 'forbidden'.

nodes.title: ANSSI-PG-083 v3.00 (2026-03-20): pure ML-KEM and pure ML-DSA, ANY parameter set, are NON-CONFORMANT; hybrid required for PQ claims
nodes.summary: France's first quantum-aware algorithm-selection guide states that ML-KEM used without hybridisation, whatever the parameter set, does not meet the asymmetric-security rule; same for ML-DSA. SLH-DSA (and hash-based) conformant alone and usable after 2030. Directly contradicts a pure ML-KEM-1024 (CNSA 2.0) TLS profile for the French market.
nodes.specifics: FR originals read via pdftotext. PG-083 3.00 p34: 'Utilisé sans hybridation et quel que soit le jeu de paramètres utilisé, le mécanisme d'encapsulation de clés ML-KEM ne respecte pas la règle RègleSécuAsym'; p36 same for ML-DSA. ML-KEM-512 conformant if hybridised with classical (ML-KEM-768 'préférable'); Frodo-KEM-640 hybridised ok (976 préférable). Signature hybrid example: sign msg with ML-DSA then classical-sign (msg,sig) (nested, differs from BSI concatenation). SLH-DSA conformant standalone; hybrid optional for hash-based. Classical ECC conformant: FRP256v1, P-256/384/521, B-283/409/571, brainpoolP256/384/512r1; Curve25519/Ed25519 not enumerated in PG-083 (ANSSI TLS guide v1.2 of 2020-03-26 calls x25519/x448 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 'acceptable'; it has no PQ content = stale). RecoSécuLongTerme: use beyond 2030-01-01 or retroactive attack risk => aim for PQ. Avis 2023-12-21: hybrid mandatory for phase-2 PQ security visas, optional in phase 3; ML-KEM main KEM, FrodoKEM encouraged. Secondary (postquantum.com updated 2026-10-11, Clubic): PQC obligation for qualification entry from 2027, 'unreasonable to buy non-PQC after 2030', first 2 PQ visas Oct 2025 (Thales card, Samsung chip, CEA-Leti) - no implementing text seen (grade C for the 2027 date).
nodes.overclaim_risk: 2027 qualification date is from press/secondary; 'mandatory hybrid' for qualification not confirmed by an implementing text.
nodes.underclaim_risk: PG-083 is a guide for qualified/certified products (RGS/CSPN/qualification), not a ban on pure ML-KEM in all French systems.

nodes.title: ASD ISM Sept 2026: ML-KEM-1024/ML-DSA-87 preferred, 768/65 sunset 2030, ECDH/ECDSA/RSA not approved beyond 2030, hybrid 'not recommended but not prohibited', no SLH-DSA/LMS/XMSS, TLS AES-GCM
nodes.summary: Australia is the strictest on algorithms and dates: all traditional asymmetric (DH, ECDH, ECDSA, RSA) 'will not be approved beyond 2030'; ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA-65 'not approved beyond 2030'; new products must support ML-DSA-87+ML-KEM-1024+SHA-384/512+AES-256 by 2030 (ISM-1917). Hybrid permitted if PQ or traditional component is an AACA (ISM-1996).
nodes.specifics: Source: ASD ISM release v2026.09.4 (2026-09-03, 'Last updated September 2026'); cyber.gov.au HTML timed out from this host so the OSCAL-repo PDF was used. Approved AACA list: DH, ECDH, ECDSA, ML-DSA, ML-KEM, RSA; SHA-2 (SHA-3 only inside ML-DSA/ML-KEM); AES. No SLH-DSA, LMS or XMSS in the list. ISM-1995 (Dec-24): ML-KEM-768 or -1024, preferably 1024. ML-DSA-65/87 approved, 87 preferred, hedged preferred, pre-hash allowed with SHA-384/512; ML-DSA-44 not approved. ISM-1917 rev3 (Sep-25): support ML-DSA-87, ML-KEM-1024, SHA-384, SHA-512, AES-256 by no later than 2030. ISM-2073 (Sep-25): PQC transition plan. ISM-1996 (Dec-24): hybrid allowed when PQ or traditional or both is an AACA. TLS: ISM-1139 TLS 1.3 only, ISM-1369 AES-GCM (ChaCha20-Poly1305 not listed), ISM-1372 (rev4 Sep-26) ephemeral DH/ECDH, ISM-1453 PFS. Consequence: X25519MLKEM768 is not ISM-compliant past 2030 (768 + X25519); SecP384r1MLKEM1024 stays compliant via ISM-1996; pure MLKEM1024 also compliant.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Secondary summary (postquantum.com) claiming ASD milestones end-2026/end-2028 not found in ISM text; do not repeat.
nodes.underclaim_risk: ASD guidance binds Commonwealth entities; private sector uses it as de facto baseline.

nodes.title: ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v3 DRAFT (Apr/May 2026, public review to end-Jul 2026) lists SecP256r1MLKEM768, X25519MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024 as Recommended; v2 (adopted mid-2025) had no TLS hybrid groups
nodes.summary: The EU certification (EUCC/Common Criteria) crypto baseline: ML-KEM and FrodoKEM 'R' but 'shouldn't be used standalone, combine with classical'; ML-KEM-1024 or 768; ML-DSA-87 or 65, SLH-DSA, XMSS/LMS R. v3 draft adds TLS 1.3 group table with all three RFC 10024 hybrids R, X25519/X448 A, AES-256-GCM R.
nodes.specifics: v3 draft pp: Note 63 (hybridization of (M)LWE KEMs), Note 64 ML-KEM-1024 or -768, Note 65 FrodoKEM-1344/976, Note 53 sig hybridization (concatenation, all must verify), Note 55 optional hybrid for hash-based, Note 58 ML-DSA-87 or -65. TLS1.3 suites: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 R, AES_128_GCM A, AES_128_CCM A; ChaCha20 not in table. Annex C adds an update process (criteria incl. standardised, 2 years stability, >=125-bit; HQC expected later). ENISA 'Hybridization of traditional mechanisms with PQC - Standardisation Status' 30 Apr 2026 is explicitly NOT a recommendation; maps composite ML-DSA (LAMPS, at RFC Editor) and composite ML-KEM. pqc-forum critique (Bernstein, Westerbaan, Mattsson): AES-128 and RSA/ECC both level A. CEPS Task Force (2025-09-29) comments call mandating hybrid a performance/interop risk and note hybrid signatures immature.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Draft: final v3 adoption status unknown at 2026-10-25 (review closed end-Jul); ACM governs certification, not deployment.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Even as a draft it shows EU cert body converging on exactly the IETF hybrid trio.

nodes.title: CCCS ITSP.40.111 v5 (effective 2026-05-29) + ITSM.40.001 (2025-06-23): ML-KEM-512/768/1024, ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA all, LMS/XMSS; classical phase-out end-2035; ECDH only NIST P-curves
nodes.summary: Canada is the most permissive: all FIPS 203/204/205 parameter sets, no hybrid mandate, classical 'without a PQ scheme' phased out by end-2035; government roadmap: plan Apr 2026, high-priority systems end-2031, all end-2035. ECDH curves P-224(to 2030)/256/384/521 only (no X25519); EdDSA Edwards25519/448 allowed for signatures.
nodes.specifics: ITSP.40.111 v5 revision history: 2016-08-02, v2 2022-08-17, v3 2024-03-19, v4 2025-03-05, v5 effective 2026-05-29. RSA/DH modulus >=3072 by end-2030; DSA, binary curves, P-224 out by 2030. Stateful hash-based sigs only if signer can manage state (SP 800-208). ITSM.40.001 (2025-06-23) defers algorithms to ITSP.40.111; ITSP.40.062 (TLS config) 'not yet updated' as of that page; CMVP-validated modules recommended.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Did not read ITSP.40.062 itself; TLS group acceptance for Canada inferred from ITSP.40.111 curve list.

nodes.title: UK NCSC: ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-65 'for most use cases'; hybrid only interim; SLH-DSA/LMS/XMSS for firmware; 2028/2031/2035 (guidance, no mandate)
nodes.summary: NCSC whitepaper v2.0 (2024-08-14) and PQC migration timelines (2025-03-20): discovery/plan by 2028, high-priority by 2031, complete 2035; hybrid acceptable only as stepping stone with path to PQC-only; hybrid authentication has no consensus, prefers single migration to PQ PKI. An industry task force claims UK 'now only recommends standalone' - not supported by the primary text.
nodes.specifics: Pages fetched via summarizer (not raw); schema dateModified 2026-04-10 / 2026-08-03 differs from visible dates => possible unseen edit. All parameter sets acceptable up to OFFICIAL.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Possible silent 2026 edits; recheck raw page.

nodes.title: EU NIS Cooperation Group PQC roadmap Part 1 v1.1 (2025-06-11): national plans by 2026-12-31, high-risk by 2030, rest by 2035; hybrid 'whenever feasible'; no algorithm list; no 2026 follow-up found
nodes.summary: 'Quantum-vulnerable public-key mechanisms shall not be used stand-alone after end of 2030' (high risk) / 2035 (medium); recommends standardised, tested hybrid; defers algorithms to ECCG ACM; CRA applies 2027-12-11. Binding layer is NIS2 transposition + CRA + EUCC, not the roadmap.
nodes.specifics: ec.europa.eu returned 403; read a mirrored PDF identical in title/version. A single secondary source claims a Jan 2026 Commission proposal to write PQC into NIS2 (unverified).

nodes.title: China ICCS/NICCS NGCC: Round 1 published 2026-09-20 (34 sigs, 41 KEMs, 9 key-exchange, 35 hashes); heavy early breakage; no mandated NIST-algorithm use and no national standard before ~2029
nodes.summary: China runs its own global PQC competition (launched 2025-02-05; PK call 2025-10-09; deadline 2026-06-30) and is not adopting ML-KEM/ML-DSA officially. Independent ngcc.dev (Saarinen) logged 104 findings against 65 of 119 candidates within three days, several design-level breaks (Tins, Facto-DSA-128, MoFang, Neulaser, FlexTree).
nodes.specifics: Counts verified: niccs list channel articleCount 34/41/9 = 84 PK. Next-round schedule not published. Wang Xiaoyun estimate (Mar 2026): national PQC standards within three years. Chinese-language search for a CAC/OSCCA migration mandate found only vendor material; no OSCCA PQC deadline located. For the golden: China market would need SM2/SM3/SM4 (TLCP/GB/T 38636 family, not re-verified this round) plus a future NGCC KEM/sig; cannot be satisfied by ML-KEM/ML-DSA alone. Treat as an out-of-scope, feature-flagged profile.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Breakage counts from a single AI-assisted sweep + secondary article.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Absence of mandate may be a search-coverage artefact (Chinese gov sources thinly indexed).

nodes.title: IANA TLS group 4590 (0x11EE) curveSM2MLKEM768 registered via draft-yang-tls-hybrid-sm2-mlkem-03, Recommended=N, DTLS-OK=N
nodes.summary: The only China-aligned TLS hybrid in the registry combines SM2 ECDH with NIST ML-KEM-768; registry confirms vendor claims of an official code point but it is a draft, not recommended, and not a Chinese national standard.
nodes.specifics: Registry rows (fetched 2026-10-25): 4587 SecP256r1MLKEM768 N RFC 10024; 4588 X25519MLKEM768 Y; 4589 SecP384r1MLKEM1024 N; 4590 curveSM2MLKEM768 N draft; 512-514 pure MLKEM N [RFC-ietf-tls-mlkem-10]; 4585/4586 ML-KEM-512 hybrids (drafts).

nodes.title: US EO 14412 (2026-06-22): HVA/high-impact systems PQC key establishment by 2030-12-31, signatures by 2031-12-31; FAR rule for contractors to comply with PQC FIPS by 2030-12-31; State Dept to push foreign governments toward NIST algorithms
nodes.summary: New US federal law-adjacent baseline (not in map). Defines PQC as resistant to both classical and quantum attack (does not require pure). Sec 5(b) diplomacy toward NIST-standardised PQC sets up friction with BSI/ANSSI hybrid-only, KpqC and NGCC.
nodes.specifics: Federal Register Vol 91 No 121, 25 Jun 2026, p38483-38486, FR Doc 2026-12909. Sec 4(b) excludes National Security Systems (NSA/CNSS track). 6(b) CMVP acceleration in 180 days; 6(c) FAR proposed rule in 180 days (due ~2026-12-19); 5(d) CBOM guidance in 270 days. OMB M-26-15 only via secondary sources.

nodes.title: Japan 2026: CRYPTREC list revised to add a PQC list containing ML-KEM (steering meeting 2026-03-30); gov target ~2035 with roadmap in FY2026; Cybersecurity Strategy 2025-12-23
nodes.summary: Extends r2e11.kpqc-korea-japan: Japan adopts NIST algorithms (ML-KEM approved into CRYPTREC; ML-DSA/SLH-DSA under evaluation), allows PQC+classical 'in combination' depending on environment, no parameter-set restriction found, roadmap due FY2026.
nodes.specifics: Language ja read. Interim report 2025-11-20 (関係府省庁連絡会議, 2nd mtg 2025-11-19); cabinet Cybersecurity Strategy 2025-12-23: migrate 'in principle by 2035', roadmap in FY2026. CRYPTREC guideline PQC FY2024 edition (Mar 2025). NICT survey: server-side PQC lags client-side.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Param sets/hybrid rules for the PQC list not read (list itself not fetched).

nodes.title: Korea 2026: Quantum Technology Industry Act Art. 18-2 obliges >600 public bodies to plan/implement PQC (cabinet 2026-05-12, effective ~Nov 2026); 3 KCMVP PQC modules validated
nodes.summary: Extends r2e11.kpqc-korea-japan with dated specifics from Korean-language press (secondary). KCMVP-validated PQC modules: Hancom/SoftForum 2025-01, XGate 2026-04, ITCS PNS 2026-07; algorithms not stated; 2035 target from 2023 master plan.
nodes.specifics: One article says KCMVP PQC validation 'from 2029' - conflicting, unresolved.

nodes.title: rustls 0.23.46 aws_lc_rs::kx_group has SECP256R1MLKEM768 and X25519MLKEM768 but NOT SECP384R1MLKEM1024 - the one hybrid group that satisfies every non-China jurisdiction
nodes.summary: docs.rs enumerates 7 statics: MLKEM768, MLKEM1024, SECP256R1, SECP256R1MLKEM768, SECP384R1, X25519, X25519MLKEM768. The EU ACM v3 (R), BSI (intended), CNSA-hybrid and ASD-post-2030-hybrid path all need 0x11ED. Resolves the 'verify' note on crate-rustls-pq.
nodes.specifics: L5 artifact: implementation-phase spike (heavy.sh): implement custom rustls::crypto::kx::SupportedKxGroup for 0x11ED using aws-lc-rs ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS path) + P-384 ECDH, order per SP 800-56C (P-384 first? ML-KEM first in RFC 10024 for X25519 only - read RFC 10024 s3 before coding), or upstream PR; acceptance: handshake interop vs OpenSSL 3.5+ s_client -groups SecP384r1MLKEM1024 and BoringSSL; CI gate asserts group list in config golden. Fallback: ship 0x11EB (BSI/FIPS) + pure MLKEM1024 only.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Docs.rs for 0.23.46 only; main branch or other providers (rustls-post-quantum, rustls-openssl) not checked.

nodes.title: Curve25519/Ed25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 are NOT accepted by BSI (TLS), CCCS (ECDH), ASD (AES-GCM only); ANSSI 2020 TLS guide accepts them but PG-083 omits them
nodes.summary: Default rustls/Chrome-style config (X25519, X25519MLKEM768, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Ed25519) fails national baselines even before PQC: BSI TR-02102-2 lists only NIST/brainpool curves and AES-GCM/CCM; CCCS ECDH curves P-224..P-521; ASD ISM-1369 AES-GCM; ECCG ACM lists X25519 as 'A' (agreed) and ChaCha absent from TLS table. Compliance profile must disable them.
nodes.specifics: L5: typed config profiles gov-eu / gov-au / gov-us-cnsa each with explicit cipher-suite, group, sigalg allowlists; CI test enumerating ClientHello acceptance per profile.

nodes.title: Pure ML-KEM TLS draft: IESG approved 2026-09-03 as Informational (Recommended=N), in RFC Editor queue 2026-09-08 after rough-consensus call 2026-07-19
nodes.summary: Updates v.pure-mlkem-tls-draft-contested: the 'blocked' state is stale; contested (Lange, Bernstein, Kobeissi objections; IPR disclosure) but advancing. EC DG CNECT asked for consensus numbers. Pure code points 0x0200-0x0202 exist in IANA, Rec=N.
nodes.specifics: Secondary (postquantum.com, updated 2026-10-10); IESG approval not verified at datatracker.

nodes.summary: PURE vs HYBRID: US NSA CNSA pure OK/target; AU hybrid discouraged-not-banned; CA/JP/UK permit either (UK hybrid interim); DE recommends only hybrid; FR/EU treat pure ML-KEM/ML-DSA as non-conformant. ML-KEM-1024 is accepted by every jurisdiction; ML-KEM-768 sunsets 2030 in AU; ML-KEM-512 only CA (and FR if hybrid). ML-DSA-87 accepted by all; ML-DSA-44 only CA; SLH-DSA absent in CNSA and ASD; LMS/XMSS absent in ASD.

nodes.title: Golden TLS key-exchange profiles: ONE universal hybrid group (SecP384r1MLKEM1024, 0x11ED) satisfies US-civil/EU/UK/AU/CA/JP; add pure MLKEM1024 only as opt-in CNSA profile; keep X25519MLKEM768 only on a 'public-web' listener
nodes.summary: R-PQC-3 (pure-CNSA golden) FLIPS to a per-jurisdiction profile set. Pure ML-KEM-1024 is NON-conformant in FR and unrecommended in DE/EU, while hybrid SecP384r1MLKEM1024 is accepted by every jurisdiction except the CNSA 'pure' profile and China. X25519MLKEM768 fails AU after 2030, DE/FR list gaps, so it is a browser-interop group, not a compliance group.
nodes.specifics:
Profiles (typed enum, all TLS 1.3 only, AES-GCM only, no 0-RTT, ECDSA/ML-DSA sigs, no ChaCha/X25519/Ed25519 in gov profiles):
P-UNIVERSAL (default compliance): kx=[0x11ED SecP384r1MLKEM1024] ; satisfies DE(intended), FR(hybrid, P-384 conformant), EU ACM v3 R, UK, AU (ISM-1996, after 2030), CA, JP, US-FIPS (SP 800-227: both parts approved).
P-BSI-ALT: [0x11ED, 0x11EB SecP256r1MLKEM768] (BSI intends both; RHEL FIPS mode only accepts the two NIST-curve groups).
P-CNSA: kx=[0x0202 MLKEM1024 pure] ONLY (draft-becker-cnsa2-tls-profile-05), sig ML-DSA-87; breaks FR/DE/EU conformance by design.
P-PUBLIC-WEB: [0x11EC X25519MLKEM768, 0x11ED, 0x11EB, x25519, secp256r1] because Chrome/Firefox offer only 0x11EC; not claimable as AU/DE/FR compliant.
P-CN (feature flag, unverified): [0x11EE curveSM2MLKEM768] + SM2 sigs; draft-only, Rec=N.
Minimal set to cover US+EU+UK+AU+CA: {0x11ED} (+0x0202 for NSS-pure). Reversal conditions: (1) NSA states hybrid non-compliant for civil FIPS; (2) BSI 2027-01 omits 0x11ED; (3) ANSSI qualification text accepts pure ML-KEM-1024; (4) ASD drops ISM-1996.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Group acceptance for FR/UK/CA inferred from algorithm lists, not from an explicit TLS-group statement (only BSI and ECCG name groups).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Cost: 0x11ED adds ~1.5 KB vs 0x11EC ClientHello; not measured here.

nodes.title: Golden signature profiles: ML-DSA-87 is the universal level (all jurisdictions); EU/FR need composite ML-DSA-87+ECDSA-P384; SLH-DSA/LMS/XMSS for release/firmware with AU exception
nodes.summary: ML-DSA-44 is only accepted by CCCS; ML-DSA-65 sunsets 2030 in AU and is not CNSA. Pure ML-DSA is non-conformant in FR and BSI wants hybrid; SLH-DSA is accepted stand-alone by BSI/FR/EU/CA/UK but excluded by CNSA and absent from ASD ISM; LMS/XMSS accepted by BSI/FR/EU/UK/CA/CNSA, absent in ASD ISM.
nodes.specifics: Profiles: S-UNIV pure ML-DSA-87 (US/AU/CA/UK); S-EU composite ML-DSA-87 + ECDSA P-384 (BSI concatenation / ANSSI nested; check LAMPS composite draft status at RFC Editor per ENISA Apr-2026 slides; no TLS stack ships it: CEPS says OpenSSL 3.5 only supports standalone ML-DSA in TLS); S-REL release signing: SLH-DSA-SHAKE-256s or LMS/XMSS for firmware (CNSA excludes SLH-DSA; AU excludes both -> AU gets ML-DSA-87). WebPKI public-cert PQ auth remains a separate open question (r3pq.pq-auth-posture-decision).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Composite ML-DSA TLS draft is individual-status; EU composite requirement may arrive via PKI not TLS.

nodes.title: Conflicts list: ten concrete cross-jurisdiction rule collisions
nodes.summary: C1 pure vs hybrid: CNSA pure ML-KEM-1024 vs ANSSI-PG-083 (pure non-conformant), BSI (hybrid only), ECCG Note 63. C2 AU: hybrid 'not recommended' vs EU 'shall be combined'. C3 AU ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA-65 sunset 2030 vs UK recommended 768/65 and DE accepting 768/65. C4 X25519MLKEM768: IANA Recommended Y and browser default vs absent from BSI intended list, AU post-2030 non-compliant. C5 SLH-DSA: BSI/FR/EU/UK/CA accept, CNSA/ASD exclude. C6 LMS/XMSS: ASD lacks vs all others accept. C7 ML-DSA-44: only CA accepts. C8 curves: BSI/CCCS/ASD NIST/brainpool vs ECCG A for X25519; ChaCha20 excluded by ASD/BSI. C9 classical sunset: AU 2030 (hard), DE 2031/2035, FR 2030 recommendation, CA 2035, EU 2030 high-risk/2035, US EO 2030/2031.
